name: addons-ios
description: iOS, behaviorally parallel to the proven test-cases/addons.json (Android), authored from the same plain-language narrative (login -> dismiss post-login dialogs/tutorial -> view Add-ons -> log out). test-cases/addons.json's resolvedSelector/selector/expect values are Android-specific (UiAutomator2 xpath, Android resource-ids, Android's permissioncontroller package) and do not apply on iOS's XCUITest tree, so none of them are carried over or guessed at here -- every step relies on instruction text for Phoenix's semantic-resolution layer (generation/semantic-act.js) to resolve at runtime against the real iOS element tree. RUN 1 (addons-run-ios-docker-1.log, real MyYes_19.3.11.ipa on BrowserStack App Automate, iPhone 15/iOS): FAILED at the original step 0 -- 'snapshot does not contain any element labeled LOGIN button' -- because iOS shows its native notification-permission alert immediately on first launch, before login, unlike Android where the equivalent dialog appears post-login (addons.json steps 8-9). Fixed by adding a new optional dismiss-notification-dialog step at index 0, ahead of the login attempt, from that real evidence. RUN 2 (addons-run-ios-docker-2.log): bug #1's fix was never actually exercised to a verdict -- the run failed on the very next step, 'tap the LOGIN button on the home screen to open the login form', with the resolver declining and reporting that the only 'LOGIN'-named elements belonged to an unrelated 'Login More Menu New' button. The real captured page-source XML proved a plain, visible, accessible, genuinely unambiguous LOGIN button WAS present and unrelated to that other button -- the bug was in generation/semantic-snapshot.js's buildGroundedSnapshot(): iOS nests a StaticText with the identical name INSIDE the button it labels (one visual control, represented twice in the tree), and the ambiguousAccessibilityId check counted that nested StaticText as a second, independently-tappable duplicate, falsely flagging the LOGIN button (and every other labeled button on this screen -- EN, ACTIVATE SIM) as ambiguous. Fixed by only treating two same-named elements as genuinely ambiguous when neither is an ancestor/descendant of the other, so a button and its own label child no longer falsely trigger each other while two real, unrelated same-named controls (the original home-LOGIN-vs-submit-LOGIN case this flag was built for) still do. RUN 3 (addons-run-ios-docker-3.log): bug #2's fix worked -- LOGIN resolved and clicked, the phone number was typed -- but the run failed one step later on 'tap the PASSWORD tab to switch the form into password-entry mode', with the resolver declining: 'no element on the screen has this label or role'. Investigated by feeding this run's real captured XML into buildGroundedSnapshot() directly: the PASSWORD button (same nested-button-with-matching-StaticText-child shape as the LOGIN bug) IS present, correctly unambiguous, not filtered as a dead end, and resolves to a normal accessibility-id selector -- it reaches the model-facing candidate list completely intact. No code-level defect was found; this is concluded to be a model/prompting-level issue (the local Ollama model declining a correct, unambiguous match, plausibly over the instruction's word 'tab' vs. the candidate's rendered role 'Button'), not a snapshot-building or resolution-engine bug, so the step wording and resolution code were left unchanged. A regression test pinning down the code-level finding was still added. RUN 4 (addons-run-ios-docker-4.log): ran against a stale local checkout that predated bugs #2/#3's fixes (confirmed by the failure message echoing the OLD 'PASSWORD tab' wording verbatim) -- not real evidence of anything new, just a `git pull` miss. RUN 5 (addons-run-ios-docker-5.log, after re-pulling to commit 9cc0a6a): failed before the app ever reached the foreground -- the real captured page source showed the iOS App Switcher (AppSwitcherContentView/SBSwitcherWindow, a my.yes.yes4g card) still under com.apple.springboard for all three startup polls, with zero findElement/elementClick calls logged. Concluded to be a one-off BrowserStack device-state glitch, not a code or test-case defect. RUN 6 (addons-run-ios-docker-6.log) confirmed that: a plain rerun did NOT repeat the App-Switcher-stuck state -- the app launched cleanly and LOGIN resolved and clicked correctly (bug #2's fix holding) -- but it surfaced bug #4: the very next step, the optional 'retry tap LOGIN -- a no-op once the login form is already open' step (added as a direct, unverified copy of addons.json step 2's Android assumption), found the SAME real LOGIN button still present on the now-open login form and clicked it a SECOND time, submitting the form before the phone number was ever typed. The user's own screenshot of the resulting screen confirmed it: the correct Yes Number/login screen, but with a stray already-typed digit and the on-screen keyboard still up from that premature submit -- exactly explaining why the next step ('type the phone number') found no clean field to use and the run never reached PASSWORD. This is a test-case design bug, not a resolution-engine bug: unlike Android, a second LOGIN tap is NOT a safe no-op on iOS. Fixed by removing that optional retry step entirely rather than guessing at a replacement. RUN 7 (addons-run-ios-docker-7.log): bug #4's fix held -- the removed retry step didn't fire again -- but the run failed on 'type the phone number' with 'No editable input field is labeled as phone number or phone/account number', and tracing the command log showed LOGIN was clicked TWICE again anyway (same stray-digit tell as bug #4): this time the still-unverified, guessed 'close the More-menu overlay' step (which has never once found a real target in any run) mis-resolved to the real LOGIN button instead. Bug #5, two real findings: (1) that More-menu step is removed, same reasoning as bug #4's retry step -- a guessed optional step that has caused the exact same premature-submit harm twice under two different guises; (2) the real captured XML shows the phone-number TextField's own accessibility label is empty (the visible 'Yes Number' text is a separate sibling StaticText, not tied to the field), so the original wording correctly found no match -- reworded to describe the field by structural position instead of a label it doesn't have. test-cases/addons.ios.json has still not had a fully clean run -- steps through LOGIN now have real, triply-confirmed evidence behind them, but phone-number entry onward (password entry, submit, tutorial carousel, Add-ons tab, logout) remain unverified/blocked pending a run that gets past these fixes. RUN 8/9/10 (addons-run-ios-docker-8/9/10.log): closed bugs #6 (a dead decoy element with no visibility check offered to the resolver, fixed in buildGroundedSnapshot()) and the PASSWORD-button model-decline issue (resolved by pinning LOGIN/PASSWORD as resolvedSelector rather than re-litigating a confirmed-stable element via Ollama every run -- see those two steps' own notes). RUN 11 (addons-run-ios-docker-11.log), with LOGIN/PASSWORD now pinned: failed on the LOGIN step anyway, but NOT from a resolution bug -- bug #7: the optional, unpinned step-0 dismiss-notification-dialog step hit a genuine Ollama fetch abort/timeout (a thrown infra error, not a model decline -- confirmed via generation/semantic-act.js's console.warn only firing in its catch block), and being optional, that failure was silently swallowed. The notification dialog was therefore never dismissed and correctly, truthfully blocked the real LOGIN button for the very next (non-optional) step. Fixed the same way as LOGIN/PASSWORD: pinned step 0's selector too (accessibility-id "Allow", confirmed present and unambiguous in every captured XML this run), removing this step's Ollama dependency entirely so a single infra hiccup can't cascade into failing the whole run again. test-cases/addons.ios.json has still not had a fully clean run; phone-number entry onward remains unverified pending the next real run.

steps.instruction: tap Allow or Don't Allow to dismiss the notification-permission system dialog if it's open
steps.note: REAL EVIDENCE, addons-run-ios-docker-1.log: on iOS this native alert ('"MyYes" Would Like to Send You Notifications', Allow/Don't Allow) appears immediately on first app launch, before login -- not after login as on Android (see addons.json steps 8-9, where the equivalent dismiss is positioned post-login). The alert covers the whole screen, so the very first run's step 0 ('tap the LOGIN button') failed with 'snapshot does not contain any element labeled LOGIN button' -- genuinely because the login button was hidden behind this dialog, not because the app failed to launch. Added here, before the login attempt, to match iOS's actual first-launch behavior. REAL EVIDENCE, addons-run-ios-docker-11.log (bug #7): being optional and unpinned made this step silently swallow a real infra failure -- 'resolveSemanticAction failed, returning unresolved: This operation was aborted' (a thrown error from the Ollama fetch call itself, confirmed by generation/semantic-act.js only logging that console.warn in its catch block, never on a clean model decline -- i.e. this was a timeout/connection abort, not the model being asked and saying no). Because the step is optional, that failure was swallowed and the run moved on with the dialog still covering the screen, which then made the very next (non-optional) step -- 'tap the LOGIN button on the home screen' -- correctly and truthfully fail with 'No button labeled LOGIN is visible on the screen,' since the real page source at that instant was 100% the alert, nothing else. Not a repeat of any prior bug: the resolvedSelector pinning fix applied to LOGIN/PASSWORD for a different reason (a stable element not worth re-litigating via Ollama every run) applies here for an additional one -- removing this step's Ollama dependency entirely means a single infra hiccup can never again silently skip it and cascade into failing the whole run. 'Allow' chosen over 'Don't Allow' since both buttons are confirmed present and this step only needs to clear the dialog, not test either choice.

steps.instruction: tap the LOGIN button on the home screen to open the login form
steps.note: REAL EVIDENCE, confirmed across addons-run-ios-docker-2.log through -10.log: at this point in the flow (home screen, login form not yet open) the only 'LOGIN'-named element on screen is this real, visible, accessible button -- its own nested StaticText label is not an independent duplicate (bug #2's ancestor/descendant fix). Pinned as a resolvedSelector so this step resolves directly via WebDriver (engine/semantic-act-executor.js tries resolvedSelector first, see its cachedSelector handling) instead of depending on Ollama being reachable/warm for a step that has never once needed the LLM to get right. Deliberately NOT applied to the second 'tap the LOGIN button to submit the login form' step below -- that one has a genuine duplicate accessibility-id on screen at that point (the now-hidden home LOGIN button) and needs the resolver's visibility-aware disambiguation (buildIosAmbiguousAccessibilityClassChain), not a plain accessibility-id selector, which would risk re-clicking the wrong one.

steps.instruction: type the phone number into the single text field below the 'Yes Number' label (the field itself has no accessibility label, so don't require one)
steps.note: REAL EVIDENCE, addons-run-ios-docker-7.log (bug #5): removed the guessed 'close the More-menu overlay' step that used to sit here -- it never found a real target in any run and, exactly like bug #4's retry-LOGIN step, mis-resolved to the real LOGIN button and clicked it a second time, submitting the form prematurely (same tell: a stray digit left in the Yes Number field afterward). Separately, the real captured XML shows the phone-number TextField itself has an empty accessibility label (`label=""`) -- the visible 'Yes Number' text is a sibling StaticText, not programmatically tied to the field -- so the original 'phone/account number field' wording correctly found nothing labeled that way ('No editable input field is labeled as...'). Reworded to describe the field by its real structural position instead of a label it doesn't have.

steps.instruction: tap the PASSWORD button
steps.note: REAL EVIDENCE, addons-run-ios-docker-3.log (bug #3): the real element is an XCUIElementTypeButton named 'PASSWORD', correctly unambiguous and reaching the model-facing candidate list intact (confirmed by feeding the run's captured XML through buildGroundedSnapshot() directly) -- but the resolver declined with 'no element on the screen has this label or role' while the instruction said 'PASSWORD tab'. Reworded from 'tab' to 'button' to match the real rendered role, since the resolution engine itself had no defect here. REAL EVIDENCE, addons-run-ios-docker-10.log (bug #6, second half): even with that 'button' wording, the resolver declined AGAIN -- 'there is no button labeled PASSWORD ... based on the snapshot provided' -- while the real captured XML, fed through buildGroundedSnapshot()/snapshotToText() directly, proves `[11] XCUIElementTypeButton "PASSWORD"` (unambiguous, no dead/expect-failed exclusion, no other PASSWORD-named control anywhere else on screen) WAS rendered into the exact candidate list the model reads. This is not a resolution-engine defect (the candidate is present and correct) -- the local Ollama model declined a clean match twice in a row, plausibly because the instruction's trailing purpose clause ('to switch the form into password-entry mode') invited it to require proof of a *behavior* no static snapshot can confirm. Rather than keep spending real BrowserStack runs re-testing the LLM's mood on an element whose selector is now confirmed stable across 3+ real runs (docker-3, -8, -9, -10), pinned it as a resolvedSelector so this step resolves directly via WebDriver, no Ollama call needed at all for it -- same reasoning as the LOGIN-button pin above.

steps.instruction: tap the password field to focus it
type the password into the password field
tap the LOGIN button to submit the login form
wait for the login submission to finish and any notification-permission dialog to appear
steps.note: Mirrors addons.json step 8's confirmed Android timing race (a variable-length spinner before the permission dialog renders). Kept as a precaution for iOS too -- unconfirmed whether the same race exists on iOS, but a fixed wait here is cheap and the Android evidence for needing one at this exact point in the flow is real.

steps.instruction: tap Allow to dismiss the notification-permission dialog if it's open
steps.note: iOS shows its own native 'App Would Like to Send You Notifications' alert with Allow/Don't Allow buttons (a system alert, not an in-app popup) -- different control from Android's permissioncontroller dialog, so addons.json's Android resource-id selector is not reused; left for semantic resolution since no real iOS alert hierarchy has been captured yet.
